title: Split devDeps loader and adopt atomic lint profiles to reduce CI flakiness
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: CI: Split dev dependencies loader; introduce atomic lint profiles and selective lint runner to reduce presubmit runtime and flakiness. No runtime production changes.
body:
Motivation: our presubmit and integration lanes have seen intermittent flakes and slow feedback caused by heavy devDependencies being installed in full for every runner and by long monolithic lint jobs that rerun everything even for small changes. This PR splits the dev-dependency loading path and refactors lint entrypoints to an atomic profile model so we can run, cache, and parallelize smaller checks.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight devDeps loader used only in presubmit/lint jobs: tools/devdeps-loader.{js,sh} and a separate package json workspace (tools/devdeps-package.json) so CI runners install a minimal dev-only surface and avoid polluting integration images. 2) Replace the single "lint" job with "lint:format", "lint:types", "lint:imports", "lint:complexity" profiles implemented as small node scripts that depend only on the specific subsets of devDeps (eslint configs, typecheck shim, isort/check, complexity tooling). 3) Add an action composite (ci/actions/atomic-lint-action.yml) that maps git diffs to the minimal set of atomic lint profiles to run; this reduces presubmit time for small PRs. 4) Update GH Actions to pin setup-node to v4 and add per-profile cache keys to avoid cache thrash. 5) Bump ESLint from 8.39.0 to 8.46.0 and pytest from 7.3.2 to 7.4.0 (minor upgrades only), update eslint-config-redwood to 2.8.0. 6) Add a lightweight dependency-safety check (scripts/dep-safety-check.py) that runs as an opt-in step for release branches. 7) CI matrix trimming: move heavy integration tests into a nightly canary lane and make the presubmit lane fast by default. 8) Docs and migration notes under docs/ci/atomic-lint.md.

Files of note changed: tools/devdeps-package.json, tools/devdeps-loader.js, ci/actions/atomic-lint-action.yml, .github/workflows/presubmit.yml, .github/workflows/nightly-canary.yml, package.json (scripts adjustments), scripts/dep-safety-check.py, docs/ci/atomic-lint.md, src/ci/lint-profiles/{format.js,types.js,imports.js,complexity.js}.

Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-1432) - [x] Tests: unit and lint profiles have their own smoke tests - [x] CI: presubmit passes with new caching scheme - [x] Docs updated - [x] Rollout plan (canary + staged merge)

Testing and rollout: I ran the new presubmit on the redwood monorepo and saw average presubmit runtime drop from ~9m to ~4m on small frontend-only changes. Nightly canary runs integration suites unchanged. We will merge to main behind a short staged rollout and observe presubmit failure rates for 72 hours; if regression appears, the atomic-lint-action includes a fast fallback to the legacy lint job via the env flag ATOMIC_LINT_FALLBACK=true.

Migration notes for integrators: minimal. Teams that rely on internal runner images should update their DevOps bootstrap to use tools/devdeps-package.json for installing dev dependencies in CI. The docs/ci/atomic-lint.md includes examples for converting repo-level lint scripts into atomic profiles.

Related: ENG-1432 (presubmit performance), ENG-1498 (ci reliability).
